sections.content: How many people stayed in Penistone after gaining qualifications?

Penistone is a small town in Yorkshire and The Humber. Penistone does not have its own university.

Penistone has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Penistone ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • fewer non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 510 state-school pupils from Penistone who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 165 (32%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 190 (37%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Penistone to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Penistone's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Penistone in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Penistone move to?

Of Penistone's graduates, 80 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

Of Penistone's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 70 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 35 of those qualified non-graduates (50%) were living fairly locally, in the Barnsley travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Penistone's GCSE cohort:

  • 35 graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber

In 2018 to 2019, 38% of graduates and 29% of qualified non-graduates living in Penistone had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 130 graduates and 170 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Penistone. This is compared with the 165 graduates and 190 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 65% of the graduates had also lived in Penistone as GCSE pupils, while 38% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Penistone in 2018 to 2019, 71% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 29% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
